claims.claim_text: The indexed Walter F. Bachelder is confirmed in a declassified 1944 personnel-interview index for the North African theater.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A declassified May 1944 index lists the exact name Walter F. Bachelder as a second lieutenant stationed at Algiers.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the exact full name and compatible commissioned Army rank in two direct wartime records, further corroborated by Dartmouth rank progression and a World War II intelligence-service obituary.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Dartmouth directories show Sergeant in 1942 and second lieutenant in 1943; the declassified theater index records second lieutenant in 1944; the OSS index records first lieutenant.
claims.match_notes: Testing Machines Inc. is explicitly postwar employment beginning in 1947 and is excluded from pre-OSS employment claims.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Albert V. Bacik probably is the U.S. Jedburgh radio operator listed with Team Arthur.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A Jedburgh roster lists the exact uncommon name Albert V. Bacik as the U.S. sergeant on Team Arthur.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable based on the exact uncommon full name, U.S. enlisted status, compatible rank, and direct OSS-SOE operational context; the corroborating roster is secondary and does not include the private identifier.
claims.temporal_assessment: The roster documents wartime Jedburgh service, not a pre-OSS employer or predecessor assignment.
claims.match_notes: The identification remains qualified pending Box 28 or an official roster with the private identifier.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Ross E. Backenstoss, Jr. probably is the Ross Elwood Backenstoss, Jr. documented at the University of Maryland in 1943.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A 1943 university commencement program supplies the exact uncommon surname, first name, middle name, and suffix; the repository also holds his 1943 thesis.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable based on exact uncommon name components and suffix plus close wartime chronology, but neither university source contains the private identifier or independently establishes OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources document university status in 1943; they do not establish when OSS service began or that student status was immediately pre-OSS.
claims.match_notes: University attendance is not classified as employment and is not claimed as an immediate pre-OSS affiliation.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Mary E. Backle is very likely the civilian secretary documented in a 1946 Strategic Services Unit successor record.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Miss Mary E. Backle, civilian Secretary
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A direct U.S. government record lists the exact uncommon name Mary E. Backle as a civilian secretary in an Athens unit reporting to SSU.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the exact uncommon name and direct placement in a documented OSS successor organization, though the 1946 record has no index identifier.
claims.temporal_assessment: The 1946 role postdates OSS and serves only as identity evidence; it is not a pre-OSS employment claim.
claims.match_notes: The later SSU secretary role is deliberately excluded from pre-OSS employer analytics.
